name: States of matter and thermal energy

questions.q: What are the three common states of matter on Earth?
Which state of matter has a fixed volume but no fixed shape, taking the shape of the container it is placed in?
How are particles arranged in a solid substance?
a: Randomly arranged with large gaps between them
Moving very fast in all directions
Tightly packed together in a regular, fixed pattern with vibrating motion
Completely free to flow past each other randomly

questions.q: Which state of matter is highly compressible because its particles are far apart and move rapidly in all directions?
What scientific term describes the change of state from a liquid to a gas?
What happens to the particles of a substance when it is heated?
a: They gain kinetic energy and vibrate or move faster, usually spreading further apart

questions.q: What term is given to the change of state directly from a solid to a gas without becoming a liquid first?
What is thermal energy?
a: The electrical charge of an object
The speed of light through a vacuum
The physical weight of a substance
The total kinetic and potential energy of all the particles inside a substance

questions.q: What is the primary method of thermal energy transfer through solid materials?
Why are metals much better thermal conductors than wood or plastic?
a: Metals contain delocalized free electrons that can collide with ions and transfer thermal energy rapidly

questions.q: What method of thermal energy transfer occurs in fluids (liquids and gases) due to differences in density caused by heating?
What term describes materials such as wool, polystyrene, or fiberglass that are poor conductors of thermal energy and used to prevent heat loss?
What happens to warm air or warm water during a convection current?
a: It expands, becomes less dense, and rises
It contracts, becomes denser, and sinks

questions.q: What type of heat transfer does not require any particles or medium to travel through and can even pass through a vacuum?
What is the temperature at which a solid turns into a liquid called?
Why do railway tracks have small expansion gaps left between sections of metal rails?
a: To allow water to drain away easily
To make the train ride bumpier
To allow the metal to expand safely on hot summer days without buckling

questions.q: What happens to water when it freezes into ice at 0 degrees Celsius?
a: It expands slightly in volume as ice crystals form a structured open lattice
It contracts continuously until it disappears

questions.q: What is the process called when a gas turns back into a liquid, such as water vapor forming droplets on a cold window?
According to the particle model of matter, why can liquids flow and take the shape of a container while solids cannot?
a: Liquid particles are held in rigid fixed positions
Liquid particles have weaker forces between them, allowing them to slide past each other
Liquid particles have turned into gases

questions.q: Which color and texture of a surface is the best absorber and emitter of thermal infrared radiation?
What scientific term describes the continuous process where warm liquid or gas rises, cools at the top, becomes denser, and sinks back down?
Why do gases fill up any container they are placed in, no matter its size?
a: Gas particles move rapidly in all directions with large spaces between them and no strong bonds
Gas particles attract the container walls magnetically

questions.q: What is the boiling point of pure water under standard atmospheric pressure?
How does a vacuum flask (thermos) minimize heat transfer by conduction and convection through its walls?
a: By using thick solid iron walls
By filling the gap with boiling water
By having a double-walled glass container with a vacuum between the walls

questions.q: What happens to the temperature of water while it is actively boiling at its boiling point?
a: The temperature stays constant until all the liquid turns into gas

questions.q: Which of the following everyday observations is caused by thermal expansion?
a: Ice melting in a glass of juice
Sagging overhead power lines on a hot afternoon
Puddles drying up on a sunny day

questions.q: Why does blowing across the surface of a hot bowl of soup help to cool it down faster?
a: It adds cold atoms to the soup
It sweeps away warm water vapor molecules just above the surface, increasing the rate of evaporation

questions.q: What state of matter is characterized by having neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume, and fills its entire container?
Why do double-glazed windows help keep houses warm in winter?
a: The trapped layer of air or gas between the two glass panes acts as a poor thermal conductor, reducing heat loss
Air is an excellent conductor of heat
It lets convection currents escape outside

questions.q: What is the term for the energy required to change a substance from a solid to a liquid at its melting point?
In an experiment testing thermal insulation, which material would cause hot water in a beaker to cool down the slowest?
a: A thin sheet of bare aluminum foil
A thick layer of bubble wrap or wool lagging

questions.q: What happens to the density of most substances when they are heated?
a: Density decreases because the particles spread out, increasing volume
